newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee project plans "fair" Christmas sales.
newsitem.headline: German coffee project plans "fair" Christmas sales.

text.p: Germany's TransFair project said on Wednesday it would launch a Christmas sales campaign of so-called fairly priced coffee, chocolate and tea.

Managing director Dieter Overath said by phone after a press conference, "Our volunteers will offer them at non-commercial events and, where possible, in supermarkets and they will inform consumers about our aim to support smallholder co-operatives in developing countries."
"Alternatively, they will ask supermarkets to put fair trade goods on their shelves."
Members of the 36 organisations supporting TransFair would be able to reach millions of consumers with their direct action.
TransFair roasted coffee sales in 1996 would be slightly higher although the overall coffee market was merely flat.
Its coffee market share should stay at around one percent.
Overath also said some 10,000 outlets would stock TransFair chocolate in the fourth quarter after a campaign launched in February had worked its way through the wholesale sector.
TransFair's tea market share in 1996 would exceed three percent this year after 2.3 percent in 1995.
